newsitem.title: USA: Muni market warns Treasury of loophole in SLGS reg.
newsitem.headline: Muni market warns Treasury of loophole in SLGS reg.

text.p: Municipal bond market participants warned U.S. Treasury Department Tuesday that a loophole in its revised state and local government series (SLGS) program could lead to abuses by municipalities if uncorrected.

"We want to call your attention to a potential use of the SLGS program that has arisen as a result of the changes made in the regulations and that we believe was unintended," the nine groups, including issuers, dealers, bond lawyers and others, said in a three-page letter to Roger Anderson, deputy assistant secretary for federal finance.
Treasury on Oct 21 issued final regulations designed to make the SLGS program easier and less costly for state and local governments that want to refinance and invest proceeds from tax-exempt bonds.
The groups noted that the new SLGS rules reduce significantly the time periods for subscribing to and cancelling SLGS orders and eliminate a requirement that SLGS cancellations be based on "cause."

They warned that as a result, there is no penalty attached to subscribing for SLGS up to 60 days period to a scheduled delivery date, and then canceling the subscription within five to seven days of the scheduled delivery date.

"This allows the SLGS program to be used to create an 'option' or 'hedge' on interest rates, with no penalty to the SLGS subscriber," they said. For example, "a municipality could apply for SLGS for a new refunding escrow and simultaneously pruchase open market securities, and then at the five/seven day deadline make a similar determination," the groups said.
The groups said Treasury could address the problem by simply invoking a section of the SLGS rules that authorizes the department's secretary to refuse a single or class of SLGS applications.

Signing the letter were representatives from Goldman, Sachs & Co.; Palmer & Dodge; Jones Hall Hill & White; New York City; the state of Pennsylvania; PSA The Bond Market Trade Association; National Association of Bond Lawyers; Government Finance Officers Association; and Public Resources Advisory Group.
